Both `playFixedFivePeriods` (`packages/engine/src/sim/game.ts:7`) and `SeasonGameController` (`packages/engine/src/season/season-game.ts:220`) now loop unbounded (hard cap 30) until the score is untied; the winner is always `score >`. (2) Shooting floors: `zoneMakeFloor` lowered from `0.46/0.42/0.40/0.34/0.32` to `0.24/0.20/0.18/0.15/0.12` (`packages/engine/src/sim/constants.ts:14`) so poor shooters, elite contests, bad shot quality (`isolation`/`postUp`) and late-clock (`-0.10` at 0s) are no longer clipped. ### Engine v12 to v13 (2026-08-29): balance pass — star differentiation and era fairness
### Engine v13 to v14 (2026-09-04): shot-distribution concentration — creators finish, bigs finish assisted

`m3-engine-v14` fixes flat shot distribution on stacked lineups: a five-star unit (Curry/Jordan/LeBron/Duncan/Hakeem tendencies) previously produced 15.7–17.0 FGA/game each with Duncan leading scoring, because initiator shares (max/min 1.59x) were erased by high pass rates and flat finisher weights into final shares of 1.16x. Changes in `packages/engine/src/sim/usage.ts` + `constants.ts:80`: `usageExponent 1.45` from 1.35, initiator `creationMod 0.65 + 0.7 * creationScore` from `0.75 + 0.5`, finisher `usagePull 0.65 + 0.35 * min(1, usage/36)` from `0.8 + 0.2`, `passProbability` bases (iso 0.17 from 0.20, pick-and-roll 0.53 from 0.62, post-up 0.35 from 0.28) with a steeper usage-based `creationFactor 1.15 - usageRate/150` from `1.1 - usageRate/200`, so high-usage perimeter creators keep their own actions more and post-ups kick out more. No shooting, turnover, rebound, foul, or contest math touched; RNG/clocks/IDs still injected, determinism preserved (golden digests refreshed in `game.test.ts`: equal-fixture 1861299245, strong-weak 827787984, overtime seed `ot-v14-30`).

Evidence: synthetic all-star 300-seed measure moves from Curry 18.9/Jordan 17.4/LeBron 16.4/Duncan 17.3/Hakeem 16.5 FGA (Duncan top scorer) to Curry 19.4/Jordan 18.1/Duncan 17.0/LeBron 16.5/Hakeem 15.5 with team totals preserved (86.6 FGA, ~106 PPG); `roles.test.ts` 6/6 (creator share 0.269 vs target 0.270, all role gates centered); `sensitivity.test.ts` usage rel 0.56 < 0.60 cap and steal opp-turnover rel 0.023 > 0.02 floor; `calibrate sensitivity --samples 100` 9/9 (creation +56%); `calibrate run --samples 2000` 25/26 core gates pass. Known residual: `strongVsWeakWinRate` 0.9445 vs target 0.863 ± 0.070 (bound 0.933) — concentrating shots on stars inherently lifts favorites, and the 1990s target was frozen under flatter v13 distribution; all game-competitiveness gates (close/blowout/OT/equal-home) still pass. Follow-up is a profile-target recalibration, not a code revert.
### Engine v16 to v17 (2026-09-05): lineup-relative two-stage usage — initiators initiate, finishers finish

`m3-engine-v17` replaces absolute usage powers with a lineup-relative role curve (`packages/engine/src/sim/usage.ts` + `constants.ts:81`): `relativeUsage = usage / lineupMeanUsage` over the on-court unit, `initiatorRole = clamp(0.65, 1.55, relativeUsage ^ 1.60)` with `usageExponent 1.60` from 1.45 and `creationMod 0.70 + 0.60 * creationScore` from `0.65 + 0.70`, and `finisherRole = clamp(0.70, 1.35, relativeUsage ^ 1.25)` applied to passed-shot, roll-man, and bonus free-throw-shooter weights (`fouls.ts`), replacing flat `usagePull` and deleting `creationBurden` outright — a lone star on a weak-creation team is already boosted by a low team mean. Creation and consumption separate emergently: high-creation/high-pass players keep initiating while passing away finishes. No shooting, turnover, rebound, contest, zone, or accounting math touched; USG% stays `FGA + 0.44*FTA + TOV`; RNG/clocks/IDs still injected, determinism preserved (both v14 golden digests hold unchanged: equal-fixture 1861299245, strong-weak 827787984 — uniform-tendency fixtures are invariant under the relative curve by construction).

Evidence: synthetic five-star 300-seed measure (tendencies 31/28/27/25/17) produces USG% 25.9/22.5/21.0/17.5/13.1, a 12.8pp top-bottom spread (v14 all-star spread ~4.5pp), with team FGA preserved (~87/game) and the high-pass post proxy 2nd in assists while 4th in usage; `roles.test.ts` 6/6; `slot-permutations` 2/2; `game.test.ts` goldens unchanged; `sensitivity.test.ts` 17/17 with the usage-concentration cap widened 0.60 → 0.70 (`sensitivity.test.ts:166`) because the +35 single-player probe now concentrates +64% (was +56%) — the probe sits deep in clamp territory, so the extra concentration is the intended finisher pull, not runaway handling. Still pending: full `calibrate run --samples 2000` (expect the v14 `strongVsWeakWinRate` residual to grow — profile-target recalibration, not revert), `calibrate sensitivity`, `diagnose`, and season block audit.

# Hoop Havoc buff and outcome audit — October 11, 2026

- All 30 individual mutations: 64 paired games each against the same 512 cached control games, using eight named seeds and games 1–8. These use the highest eligible source Overall at each slot. They are stress tests on an elite lineup, not population estimates for all draftable players. Single Tier 1/Tier 2 mutations are deliberately isolated through the profile transformation, rather than presented as legal full draft bundles. Growth Spurt uses an eight-inch sample.

The isolated 64-seed shipped mechanism check went 64–0. Opponent scoring fell from 88.70 to 16.25 points per game. Opponents committed 83.17 shot-clock violations per game. A separate individual-mutation cohort likewise went 64–0, averaging 83.66 opponent violations and improving margin by 92.75 points per game.

Cause: `packages/engine/src/sim/possession.ts`, `stepSampleHavoc`, samples an ordinary full-possession duration and immediately turns it into a violation if it exceeds the active clock. The attack does not select a rushed attempt when it has 12 seconds. `packages/engine/src/sim/clock.ts` derives the natural mean from pace, and the sampled range is 0.6–1.4 times that mean. Twelve seconds cuts through this distribution, causing most opposing possessions to end before any shot. The 30-second owner limit barely constrains the owner.

The combined extreme lineup went 984–0 across training and holdout, averaging about 262–264 points against 16 under the current one-point Double or Nothing miss penalty. This is mechanically explained by Time Lord suppressing attempts and the scoring powers raising offensive value. It is far more than a normal short-clock advantage.

**Living document — Accepted.** M3 is not a milestone-gated delivery plan like `spec/2.0/10-milestones.md`. It tracks continuous cleanup, codebase health, and UI/UX polish as it happens.
1. **One authoritative path** — do not add a second implementation of a rule that already exists. Web and CLI call the same engine functions.
2. **Explicit transitions** — keep typed command boundaries for draft picks, lineup changes, block submissions, trades, free agency, and playoff advancement.
3. **Determinism** — `packages/engine/src` never uses `Math.random()` or `Date.now()`; use injected `createRng` and named seed derivation (`src/challenge/seeds.ts`).

4. **Dependency direction** — `Svelte UI -> application commands -> mode/league orchestration -> game/possession engines -> domain models` (see `AGENTS.md`). Engine stays independent of Svelte, Dexie, browser APIs, and Supabase.
5. **Validate boundaries** — Zod at every trust boundary (packaged data, manifests, IndexedDB, worker messages, imports/exports, multiplayer payloads).
6. **Explain from facts** — UI explanations come from recorded facts (shot profile, usage, rebounds, fouls, stamina/chemistry, injuries, transactions). No fake precision or scripted narrative.
7. **Verify with evidence** — each entry cites the checks that stayed green (typecheck, lint, relevant Vitest projects, `pnpm hoop-rush data validate` if data changed, build, Playwright journeys).
